subject: Counting rules for hybrid sessions and minimums — proposal
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan@evergreen.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Kara Li <kara@evergreen.ai>
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify billing for hybrid chat + streaming sessions

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Before we move to a pilot I need to lock down how Redwood will bill our mixed workloads. We run a virtual agent that does: (1) a short interactive chat turn (user prompt + a generated reply) and (2) a downstream streaming transcription/semantic pipeline that may re-hydrate a long chat history for context. Two quick scenarios attached (sample-invoice-may.pdf) — please see the shaded rows.

Main questions:
- When we "stitch" a long history into a subsequent chat turn, do you bill the entire re-sent history tokens every call or only the delta (new tokens) when the KV/prefix cache is reusable?
- What rounding/quantum do you apply per call or per session? Do you have a minimum per-call bucket that could blow up small-turn pricing?
- For sequences where a 12k context is used but our immediate prompt + response is only ~300 tokens, how will rounding/minimums and session amortization interact?

Example numbers from our invoice: three calls in 24h that reference the same 9k history block. On paper it looks like we're being charged for the full 9k three times — that's not sustainable. Can you provide a clear counting example and any possible concession for pilot months?

Attaching sample invoice. Happy to hop on a 30 min call with procurement if needed.

Thanks,
Evan Brooks
Head of Product, Evergreen AI
E: evan@evergreen.ai | M: +1 (415) 555-0191

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing for hybrid chat + streaming sessions

Hi Evan —

Appreciate the concrete examples — that helps. Short answer: we try to avoid charging full history repeatedly when the platform can reuse KV/prefix state, but the exact accounting depends on how the calls are routed (same model variant, same region) and the TTL for cached prefix material. Below is a proposal and a worked example.

Proposal (recommended default):
- Classification: calls are either "stateless per-call" (no history pinned) or "session-anchored" (shared prefix/KV).
- Billing primitive: billable_tokens = new_input_tokens + new_output_tokens.
- Prefix reuse credit: if the platform successfully reuses cached KV for the same prefix within the policy window (configurable; default 6 hours), we do not re-bill the repeated prefix tokens — we only bill the delta tokens required to rehydrate beyond the cached offset.
- Minimums & quantum: we apply a per-call floor of 64 tokens and round up to the nearest 8-token quantum for billing transparency (this is our current hosted default). For session-anchored calls we amortize the first-call prefix allocation across subsequent calls in the same session at invoice time.

Worked example (from your invoice):
- Base history block: 9,120 tokens (9k rounded).
- Call A (first time history attached): request 120 tokens + response 280 tokens = 400 tokens. Billing: first call pays the amortized prefix load (we allocate a 2,000-token warm-up charge the first call that pulls history into runtime), plus new input/output tokens. In practice that means: charge = 2,000 (prefix warm-up) + 400 = 2,400 tokens -> rounded up to nearest 8 = 2,400 -> floor applies so no change.
- Call B (same prefix reused within 6h): request 110 + response 190 = 300 tokens. Billing: cache reuse credit applies; prefix warm-up not re-billed. charge = 300 -> rounded up to 304 (nearest 8) -> apply per-call floor (64) not relevant.
- Call C (after 12h, cache expired): behaves like Call A again.

Notes / options:
- If you want fully conservative billing (never charge full history warm-up), we can flip to delta-only billing for your pilot: only charge newly transmitted tokens (you'd see much lower first-call bill but we reserve the right to reintroduce warm-up charge at scale).
- For enterprise Dedicated customers we can set longer cache TTLs and reduce/amortize warm-up more aggressively.

Next steps: I attached a small spreadsheet (proposed-counting-matrix.xlsx) that walks through the math for your three invoice rows and two concession flavors (conservative pilot vs standard). Can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through numbers with your procurement? I copied Sergio to loop in negotiation and Ben for billing follow-up.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
T: olga@redwood.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Evan Brooks <evan@evergreen.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing for hybrid chat + streaming sessions

Evan / Olga —

Thanks for the example. Two quick thoughts on negotiation and a suggested pilot concession that Ben and I can operationalize:

1) Pilot concession (90-day): for the pilot period we can apply a "cache-first" billing mode:
   - No warm-up amortization charged on first three distinct history loads per rolling 30 days.
   - For any repeated reuse within 6 hours we credit 100% of the repeated prefix tokens (delta-only billing).
   - We will provide a one-time invoice credit equal to 50% of any billed history warm-up tokens that exceed your modeled conservative delta-only expectation for the first 30 days.

2) Long-term contractual options: if Evergreen commits to a 12-month Dedicated capacity (>X reserved units) we can:
   - Extend the prefix TTL to 72 hours and reduce the warm-up allocation to 512 tokens (instead of 2,000) for pinned histories.
   - Introduce a tiered rounding quantum (8 tokens -> 4 tokens) for high-volume customers to limit rounding overhead.

Quick sample calc (from your three calls):
- Raw billed under standard policy: 2,400 + 304 + 2,400 = 5,104 tokens (rounded examples).
- Under pilot concession (delta-only + credits): 400 + 300 + 400 = 1,100 tokens billable; plus 50% credit on any warm-up over delta model applied to first month invoice.

If this looks acceptable we will: (a) create an amendment to the SOW for the pilot (Ben will draft), (b) set the HubSpot deal to "Pilot - Cache-first billing" and (c) add a note for the infra team to set a 6h prefix TTL for the pilot.

Ben — can you draft the SOW amendment and attach to the HubSpot deal? Olga — Evan, when you confirm procurement details we'll share a DocuSign amendment link.

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
